No no, the question to ask a Canadian is if they make their own maple syrup. You're not a legitimate Canadian if you haven't.

This Canadian makes maple syrup by tapping maple trees. You want to tap them either in the early spring or fall (but not both because you'll kill the tree) because that is when the sap flows. Up in the spring to rejuvenate the tree and down in the fall when the tree enters dormancy.

You want a sugar maple tree that is at least 8 inches in diameter. You need to drill a hole into the tree that will accommodate the girth and depth of the spile you're using. Then you want to get a spile with sap tubing and set it up with a big 15 L water jug. The caps on those bottles are perfectly sized for the sap tube to go into, so I feed the tube into the top and it's nice and leak resistant.

The traditional method, while extremely picturesque, allows for wandering deer to drink all your precious sap, hence my personal setup with the jug and tube.

Then you just let the sap flow. It's best to collect it and boil it once a day otherwise it can go stagnant or ferment. Before you boil it you want to filter the sap because chunks of bark, leaves, and even bugs can get into it and contaminate your syrup.

The ratio of sap to water is 40 to 1, so if you start out with 40 litres you have to boil it down to 1 litre to have a tasty syrup. Some people who are more skilled in the art than I can keep boiling it down and get maple sugar which is pretty dang delicious too.

They call it liquid gold for a reason. The boiling is so tiresome. Like honestly, boiling and boiling and boiling on the wood stove for hours at a time for a month is a lot of work. Dragging it back from the field in thigh high snow is a lot of work. It's a seriously labourious way to get some fructose.

That's my home production method. More commercialized setups have tube networks that connect the trees directly to a giant reservoir, and they boil huge batches at a time. They also use all these fancy tools to gauge sugar content but I can't be bothered with all that as my syrup is for my enjoyment alone.
